answer:
Fixed token windows are cheap and predictable but split arguments and tables; overlap reduces boundary loss while duplicating evidence. Recursive splitting respects paragraph/heading boundaries until a size limit. Structure-aware chunks preserve sections, tables, and parent metadata. Semantic splitting groups related sentences but adds embedding cost and can still separate necessary definitions. [1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

Contextual retrieval prepends a short document-specific explanation before indexing each chunk; keep original text and provenance so generated context cannot silently become evidence. Compare alternatives on answer-bearing retrieval recall, grounded answer accuracy, citation correctness, index size, and latency. Tune chunk size jointly with reranking and context budgets. There is no universally optimal chunk length: a short factual lookup and a cross-section synthesis require different evidence granularity.
